page: Amazon Web Services r5d.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory, delivering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Storage is bundled with 300 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage, and the network configuration provides a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities across most multi-core and memory-bound workloads. The instance achieves average ratings in Passmark CPU and memory tests, as well as in Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by lower scores in stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core benchmarks. Large-block memory bandwidth reads and writes also fall into the average tier, while LLM inference speeds for medium-sized models are poor, reflecting its lack of hardware acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5d.2xlarge offers a balanced profile for memory-intensive applications that require high-speed local scratch space. The inclusion of 300 GB of local NVMe SSD storage provides a high-performance caching layer without the added cost of external block storage. However, the tradeoff lies in its older Intel Xeon architecture and modest 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, which may limit performance in highly distributed or network-bound environments.

This instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads that benefit from local, low-latency storage. Appropriate use cases include medium-sized databases, in-memory caches like Redis, data buffering, and local data processing tasks. It is less suitable for compute-heavy tasks, single-threaded applications, or large-scale machine learning inference.
